sections.h2: Why a Monroe-area seller deals with this office
sections.html:
A sale is not finished in the public record until the deed lands at the Union County Register of Deeds. That office holds the lasting record of who owns land in the county and how it changed hands: deeds, plats, powers of attorney and more.

Vital records, marriage licenses, notary oaths and passport applications are handled at the same counter. A house seller only cares about the land side. Whoever runs your closing delivers the signed deed, and its time stamp decides who ranks first if two claims collide.

The office dates to the county's formation in 1842, and the register is an elected position. Even a quick cash sale of a Union County house ends at this counter.

sections.h2: What the office can and cannot do
sections.html:
Think of this as a filing counter, not a legal help desk. State law bars the register and staff from practicing law, which means no blank legal forms and no coaching on completing one. Staff send people to an attorney.

Changing the names on a house means recording a fresh deed. An old deed is never edited.

  • Liens and judgments against a person or property: the Clerk of Court, 704-698-3100.
  • Who owns a given street address: the tax assessor, 704-283-3746, since the register indexes by name.
  • Drafting or correcting a deed: a North Carolina attorney.

sections.h2: Where to file a deed in Monroe
sections.html:
The office is in the Union County Government Center, 500 North Main Street, Monroe. Recording hours are Monday to Friday, 8 a.m. to 5 p.m. You can bring a document in or send it through an e-recording vendor. Neighborhood covenant files are kept on the second floor.

Simplifile, CSC and ePN are the vendors in use now. You arrange setup with the vendor directly, but most sellers never touch it, because the firm running a closing usually already has an account. Ask which vendor your firm uses and when the stamped copy comes back.

Paper filers bring the signed original and a check for the fee. Payment is expected at the time you hand the document over, so a package without it will not get filed. If your closing firm is handling all of this, you only need to ask for confirmation once the filing is done.

The first fifteen pages of an instrument cost $26.00, and each further page is $4.00. State law uses the same pair of numbers for instruments generally. The excise tax on deeds is $2 per thousand dollars for deeds since August 1, 1991.

sections.h2: Excise tax on a Union County deed
sections.html:
The transferor owes this tax. As written by the legislature the rate is a dollar for each $500 of value, the same as $2 per thousand, and it has to be paid ahead of recording.

In a typical sale that is the seller, shown as a line at settlement. Half the tax stays in the county general fund and half goes to the state.

The amount follows the value stated in the deed, so take the figure from your closing office.

The register's website carries deeds starting in 1973 and maps starting in 1842. Older deeds, plus every other kind of record, mean a visit in person.

Two limits catch people. The deed look-up covers deeds and plats only, so mortgage information is not there. And the index is built on names, so typing a street address into it gets you nowhere.

  • Know the owner's name as it appears on the last deed.
  • Call the assessor for the owner of a street address.
  • Go to the office for mortgages and deeds of trust.
  • Look in the same office for filed HOA covenants, if the county holds them.

A seller can use the search to confirm that the signers match the names on title and that no old deed of trust is still open.

sections.h2: Union County housing at a glance
sections.html:
The 2025 population estimate is 267,674, up 12.4 percent from the April 2020 base of 238,179, with 95,683 housing units. About 81.6 percent of homes are owner-occupied, so most sales here involve a single-family owner rather than a landlord.

The median value of an owner-occupied home is $417,300, and median household income is $102,900. Median rent is $1,496, and builders took out 2,707 permits in 2025. Median monthly owner cost is $1,940 with a mortgage and $553 without one. Steady new construction shapes who buys, and the register's index shows every deed that moves between them.

For land records, use 500 North Main Street, Suite 239, Monroe, NC 28112, telephone 704-283-3843. Mail goes to PO Box 248, Monroe, NC 28111-0248. If you deliver a deed by hand, go to Suite 239.

Most sellers skip the mail and let the closing firm file electronically.

The county also posts older excise tax rates for tracing past transfers: $1 per thousand for 1969 to July 1991 and $1.10 per thousand before 1968. They only matter if you are working through an old deed in the family chain of title.

sections.h2: Does filing order change who wins a dispute?
sections.html:
Under G.S. 47-18, a conveyance has no force against lien creditors or purchasers for value before it is registered, and rank follows registration time.

A gap between signing and filing therefore carries risk. An uncancelled deed of trust on an inherited house also deserves a look before you sign a contract. Releases record free. Keep the recorded copy with your sale papers.

Three numbers cover most questions: assessor 704-283-3746, Clerk of Court 704-698-3100 and the register's vital records line 704-283-3610.

Notary commissions are also kept here. A notary who is renewing takes the oath in person for a $10.00 fee. Have your closing office confirm that the notary witnessing your signature holds a current commission.

Probate, divorce and tax matters run through the courts and the tax office. The register files the paper they produce.

Your attorney or title firm prepares the deed, you sign it before a notary, and the firm pays the excise tax out of your proceeds. The firm then files the deed, usually electronically, and the office stamps it with the date and time. Ask for the stamped copy and keep it. If you paid off a mortgage, the satisfaction of the deed of trust records free, so confirm it is filed. For a cash sale the steps are the same, just without a lender's paperwork.

faqs.q: Is the Union County deed office open on weekends?
faqs.a: No. Hours are weekdays, 8 a.m. to 5 p.m. E-filers use Simplifile, CSC or ePN; ask the vendor about its cutoff time.

faqs.q: Will Union County staff fix a mistake in my deed?
faqs.a: No. Staff cannot advise on drafting, so the attorney who prepared the deed has to correct it.

faqs.q: How was the deed tax set before 1991?
faqs.a: It was $1 per thousand for 1969 to July 1991 and $1.10 per thousand before 1968. The rate is $2 per thousand now.

faqs.q: Why can't I type my address into the deed search?
faqs.a: The index runs on names, not addresses. Call the assessor at 704-283-3746 for an owner. Online deeds begin in 1973.

faqs.q: Do payoff releases cost extra in Union County?
faqs.a: No. G.S. 161-10 exempts satisfactions and cancellations from the fee.
